reconstructed_captions.20: The cut pieces of black leather are arranged on the work surface.
reconstructed_captions.21: A hand applies adhesive along the edge of a piece of leather.
reconstructed_captions.22: Another piece of leather is carefully placed on top of the glued edge.
reconstructed_captions.23: The two pieces are pressed together firmly to create a bond.
reconstructed_captions.24: A hand uses a wing divider to score a stitching guideline parallel to the edge.
reconstructed_captions.25: A multi-pronged pricking iron is positioned on the scored guideline.
reconstructed_captions.26: A mallet is used to strike the pricking iron, punching stitching holes through the leather.
reconstructed_captions.27: The pricking iron is moved along the guideline to create a continuous row of holes.
reconstructed_captions.28: A close-up shows the perfectly spaced stitching holes ready for sewing.
reconstructed_captions.29: Two needles are threaded with waxed thread for saddle stitching.
reconstructed_captions.30: A hand begins stitching, passing the first needle through a hole.
reconstructed_captions.31: The second needle is passed through the same hole from the opposite side.
reconstructed_captions.32: The stitching continues down the line, with the thread pulled taut after each stitch.
reconstructed_captions.33: A close-up highlights the neat, angled appearance of the saddle stitch.
reconstructed_captions.34: The final stitches are made, and the thread is secured and trimmed close to the leather.
